resources.string: Auto Lens

Launch the app or tap its Quick Settings tile to capture the screen once after a one-second delay and send it to Google Lens. Auto Lens does not monitor your screen, read the view hierarchy, or perform touch gestures. You can turn off accessibility access in Settings at any time.
Your screen.\nThrough Google Lens.
Launch once. Capture in one second. Open Lens.
One-time accessibility setup

Auto Lens uses the screenshot feature of an accessibility service. It captures one image of your current screen only when you launch the app or tap its tile. The image may include personal information visible on screen.

The image is saved in temporary app storage and shared with Google Lens. Images processed by Lens are subject to the Google privacy policy. Auto Lens itself does not send data over the internet.

If you agree, enable Auto Lens on the next Settings screen, then return to the app. Capture will start when you return.

To capture another app, add the Auto Lens tile using the Quick Settings editor. Launching from the home screen may capture your home screen after the one-second delay.
If access is blocked on Android 13 or later, open App info → top-right menu → Allow restricted settings.
